title: TAPAS: Thermal- and Power-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference in Cloud Platforms
problem: LLM inference workloads exhibit fine-grained millisecond-scale phase transitions (prefill vs. decode) with distinct thermal and power profiles, which traditional cloud thermal and power management techniques are too coarse-grained to handle effectively. Cloud co-location of SaaS and IaaS workloads with differing visibility levels further complicates scheduling.
method: TAPAS is a thermal- and power-aware scheduler for LLM inference that models the per-phase (prefill/decode) thermal and power profiles of inference workloads at millisecond granularity. It leverages LLM configuration parameters (model parallelism, model size, quantization level) as scheduling knobs to trade off performance, temperature, power consumption, and output quality. The scheduler accounts for co-located SaaS and IaaS workloads, applying different control strategies depending on the level of visibility and flexibility available for each workload type.

title: Rethinking Prefetching for Intermittent Computing
problem: Conventional hardware prefetchers are energy-wasteful on batteryless energy harvesting systems (EHSs) because they aggressively fetch cache lines that are lost on power failure before any hit, wasting harvested energy. Frequent outages on EHSs mean that prefetched data that is never accessed before the next power loss represents pure energy overhead.
method: IPEX (Intermittence-aware Prefetching EXtension) is an add-on layer that wraps existing prefetchers on EHSs without replacing them. It tracks which prefetched cache blocks receive a hit before a power failure and suppresses future prefetches of lines that historically go unused ('useless prefetches'). Additionally, IPEX monitors harvested energy levels to predict imminent outages and dynamically throttles the prefetch degree at that moment, targeting only blocks likely to be accessed before power loss. The result is that harvested energy is redirected from futile prefetches toward productive forward execution progress.

title: Orion: A Fully Homomorphic Encryption Framework for Deep Learning
problem: Mapping arbitrary deep neural networks to Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) primitives is intractable with existing tools because FHE requires packing large vectors, managing noise budget through bootstrap placement, and translating general convolutions to the limited FHE instruction set—challenges that have limited FHE neural inference to shallow or small networks.
method: Orion is an automated compiler that accepts PyTorch DNNs and emits FHE programs. It introduces a single-shot multiplexed packing strategy for arbitrary convolution layers that avoids the combinatorial explosion of prior slot-packing schemes. Orion also introduces an automated bootstrap placement algorithm with scale management that tracks noise accumulation across layers and inserts bootstrapping operations at minimum-cost positions. Together these enable end-to-end compilation of deep networks (ResNet-20, ResNet-50, YOLO-v1 with 139M parameters) without manual FHE engineering.

title: An Enhanced Data Packing Method for General Matrix Multiplication in Brakerski/Fan-Vercauteren Scheme
problem: Performing GEMM in Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is inefficient due to high computational demands, significant data migration bandwidth constraints, and incompatibility of standard activation functions with FHE schemes like BFV.
method: Introduces polynomial encoding methodology for GEMM under Brakerski/Fan-Vercauteren (BFV) scheme. Extends method to support packing inputs and weights for various matrix dimensions. Designs specialized FPGA hardware (U250) with optimized scheduling between device and host to accelerate inference via cooperative computation.

title: Efficient Security Support for CXL Memory through Adaptive Incremental Offloaded (Re-)Encryption
problem: CXL memory expansion devices adopted in cloud TEE environments (Intel SGX/TDX, AMD SEV) require XTS encryption for data confidentiality via CXL IDE, but XTS encryption's per-page latency causes significant performance overhead on memory-intensive workloads. Dynamically switching between CTR and XTS encryption modes and re-encrypting pages when access frequency changes incurs additional overhead that existing designs do not handle efficiently.
method: AIORE (Adaptive Incremental Offloaded Re-Encryption) combines CTR-mode encryption (low latency, parallelizable) for frequently accessed hot pages with XTS encryption (CXL IDE compliant) for cold pages. The framework dynamically selects the encryption scheme per page based on tracked access frequency using a lightweight monitoring mechanism. When a page's access pattern changes (cold-to-hot or hot-to-cold), AIORE performs incremental re-encryption, processing only the modified page rather than the entire memory region. Re-encryption is offloaded to computation resources within the CXL memory node itself, overlapping re-encryption with ongoing memory traffic to hide latency. The scheme is evaluated using gem5 full-system simulation across diverse benchmarks.

title: Practical Federated Recommendation Model Learning Using ORAM with Controlled Privacy
problem: Federated learning (FL) for recommendation models is impractical because the large embedding tables require each user to access a tiny fraction of table entries, and hiding those access patterns via ORAM incurs prohibitive latency and SSD wear. Existing ORAM-based approaches have latency and SSD lifetime overheads that make them undeployable at scale.
method: FEDORA places the large ORAM structure on SSDs rather than DRAM, using SSD-friendly access optimizations to reduce write amplification and wear. It introduces epsilon-FDP (Federated Differential Privacy), a formal framework that trades off ORAM privacy strength against performance by allowing a controlled, quantified privacy budget, reducing the number of ORAM operations required. The system also supports modern FL operation modes (e.g., asynchronous and partial participation) so it integrates with production FL pipelines.

title: VEDA: Efficient LLM Generation Through Voting-based KV Cache Eviction and Dataflow-flexible Accelerator
problem: LLM inference on edge devices faces memory and computational bottlenecks due to intensive KV cache requirements and variable sequence lengths, limiting deployment feasibility.
method: Algorithm-hardware-dataflow tri-optimization: (1) voting-based KV cache eviction identifies unimportant kv vectors adaptively, reducing cache size while maintaining accuracy; (2) flexible-product dataflow with runtime-reconfigurable PE array handles diverse matrix-vector dimensions; (3) element-serial scheduling for nonlinear ops (softmax, layernorm). Hardware complexity reduced from O(N) to O(1). Custom VEDA accelerator implementation.

title: Hydra: Scale-out FHE Accelerator Architecture for Secure Deep Learning on FPGA
problem: Existing FHE accelerators for deep learning focus on single-node throughput by stacking parallelized compute clusters, which cannot leverage application-level parallelism across model layers and are not scalable beyond a single card for increasingly large models.
method: Hydra partitions the deep learning model (CNN and LLM layers) across multiple FPGA-based server nodes, each handling a portion of the model governed by a central scheduling mechanism on the host server. The architecture supports multi-server scaling with theoretically arbitrary numbers of compute nodes, enabling pipeline parallelism at the model level in addition to intra-node parallelism. Hydra achieves scale-out by distributing ciphertext operations across nodes with the host managing data routing and synchronization.

title: HStencil: Matrix-Vector Stencil Computation with Interleaved Outer Product and MLA
problem: Stencil computations are fundamental HPC kernels but suffer from underutilized matrix units, limited instruction-level parallelism, and poor cache hit rates when working sets exceed cache capacity. Existing approaches fail to fully exploit modern matrix-unit capabilities.
method: HStencil introduces three optimizations: 1) Microkernels jointly leveraging matrix and vector units, 2) Fine-grained instruction scheduling with interleaved execution for instruction-level parallelism, 3) Spatial prefetch to sustain performance when working sets exceed cache capacity.

title: 5.8 A 20W CMOS/LDMOS All-Digital Transmitter with Dynamic Retiming and Glitch-Free Phase Mapper, Achieving 68%/62% Peak Drain/System Efficiency
problem: Base stations dominate wireless operator energy consumption (73%); analog PA-based transmitters suffer from high quiescent currents and limited bandwidth, but achieving high-power all-digital transmitters (DTX) at mMIMO levels (>3W) requires fine gate segmentation and glitch-free operation for wideband modulation.
method: 8-phase multi-phase digital upconversion transmitter with dynamic retiming and glitch-free phase-mapper; custom low-VT LDMOS MMIC with power switch banks featuring in-finger gate segmentation and high-density flip-chip DTX controller integration.

title: MXBLAS: Accelerating 8-bit Deep Learning with a Unified Micro-Scaled GEMM Library
problem: Current MX-GEMM implementations are model-oriented with rigid problem-kernel coupling, inefficient promotion operations, and overlooked quantization overhead.
method: MXBLAS: template-based MX-GEMM library; adaptive runtime kernel generation; compute-store co-optimization fusing quantization into epilogue.

title: DuRTL - Information Flow Analysis Tool for Register Transfer Level Hardware Designs
problem: Understanding and comprehending unknown or legacy hardware designs written in Verilog/VHDL is challenging. Information flow tracking is critical for security analysis, verification, and design understanding but lacks accessible tools.
method: DuRTL implements Hardware Information Flow Tracking (IFT) using tagging mechanism. Unique tags injected into hardware designs; each tag associates a signal at a specific time with information flow during circuit traversal.

title: LIO-DPC: Accurate and Fast LiDAR-Inertial Odometry with Dynamic Pose Chain
problem: LiDAR-inertial odometry must balance speed and accuracy: filter-based methods are fast but suffer from cumulative errors; graph-based methods reduce errors but are computationally expensive, making real-time operation challenging.
method: LIO-DPC combines filter-based and graph-based approaches using a dynamic pose chain. A fast filter generates initial poses, then computationally efficient local graph optimization refines relative poses on local pose chains. Loop sparsification selects representative loops (temporally and spatially proximate) to reduce graph complexity while minimizing loop errors.

title: TaOPT: Tool-Agnostic Optimization of Parallelized Automated Mobile UI Testing
problem: Parallelizing automated mobile UI testing across multiple test devices is inefficient because existing tools explore overlapping UI subspaces on different devices, wasting resources by redundantly testing similar app states. No existing approach optimizes the parallelization of arbitrary automated UI testing tools without modifying their internal workflow.
method: TaOPT performs online UI subspace inference by analyzing the App Under Test (AUT) to identify loosely coupled UI subspaces—regions of the app's state graph that can be explored independently. TaOPT then coordinates access to these subspaces across different testing devices, guiding each device's testing tool toward distinct, unexplored subspaces without modifying the tool's internal search logic (tool-agnostic). This subspace partitioning and assignment is updated dynamically as testing progresses, using observations of which subspaces each device has covered to avoid redundancy. By separating exploration across devices at the subspace granularity, TaOPT maximizes coverage diversity.

title: Integrating Distributed SQL Query Engines with Object-Based Computational Storage
problem: Object storage systems (S3, MinIO) support only basic in-storage filtering, forcing complex operators (aggregation, top-N) to execute at compute layer, causing excessive data movement and query latency.
method: Presto-OCS connector analyzes distributed SQL execution plans to identify operator pushdown eligibility. Offloads complex operators (aggregation, top-N, joins) to OCS for in-storage execution. Evaluated on real-world HPC analytics queries and TPC-H benchmark.

title: MANS: Efficient and Portable ANS Encoding for Multi-Byte Integer Data on CPUs and GPUs
problem: Asymmetric Numeral Systems (ANS) is a high-ratio, high-throughput lossless compression algorithm but lacks effective support for multi-byte data and cross-platform (CPU/GPU) compatibility. Multi-byte data compression remains suboptimal.
method: MANS introduces Adaptive Data Mapping (ADM) scheme that maps multi-byte integers to single-byte space based on data characteristics, preserving ANS efficiency. Separate optimization for CPU and GPU architectures combined into portable pipeline.
